subject: [Escalation] QPS curtailment causing latency & 429s — exec attention requested
messages:
From: Jake Morris <jake.morris@streamlinehealth.com>

Cc: tina.park@streamlinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 08:17:12 -0800
Subject: Major latency spike + 429s impacting production (region: us-west)

Hi Vivek,

We started seeing latency spikes and a bunch of 429s hitting our inference endpoints from this morning (08:00 PST onward). Overall throughput for our main workflow dropped ~40% and customers are seeing timeouts inside our service.

Quick context: we've been migrating 80% of traffic to the dedicated endpoint you provisioned (model: rdw-base-1.2) and our normal QPS is ~120 sustained with short bursts to 400 for short windows. This morning we saw a sudden cap down to ~30-40 QPS and a sustained 429 rate for ~90 minutes.

Attached are a sample of logs and a small flamegraph from our side. Can Redwood confirm whether anything changed on your quota/burst side or if routing/fallback kicked in? This is P1 for us — we need help ASAP.

Thanks,
Jake
Ops Lead, Streamline Health

Attachments: server_logs_sample.txt (attachment stub)

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai

Subject: INTERNAL: Streamline Health P1 — sudden QPS reduction & 429s (prep for 09:00 triage)

Team — looping you in. Summary from the customer: sustained drop from ~120 QPS -> ~30 QPS, many 429s from 08:00–09:30 PST. Customer on dedicated capacity (dedicated-pool-12), model rdw-base-1.2.

Ask: please prioritize a quick root-cause sweep before the call:
1) Check quota window and burst policy evaluations for dedicated-pool-12 between 07:45–09:15 PST.
2) Check smart routing fallbacks and whether requests were routed to lower-capacity variant.
3) Validate that compilation/kernel selection didn't cause a regression for sequences >1024 tokens (customer mentioned longer requests last night).

Marcus — confirm SLA/discount posture if we need to offer credits.
Neha — can you pull the policy snapshots and any throttle logs? Attach to the Jira (SUP-2143).

I'll be on the triage call at 09:00.

— Vivek

From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 10:12:03 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: Streamline Health P1 — initial findings (quota window mis-eval)

On Tue, Nov 7, 2028 at 08:35 AM Vivek wrote:
> Team — looping you in. Summary from the customer: sustained drop from ~120 QPS -> ~30 QPS...

Quick findings from the triage:
- We observed that the dedicated-pool-12 quota evaluator applied a per-minute smoothing window incorrectly: a recent config change (rollout id cfg-20281106-quiet) adjusted the burst-accounting to a 5m decay but the code path that reconciles per-customer reserved tokens used a 60s window. The mismatch caused the effective instantaneous allowance to be ~25% of expected during repeated short bursts.
- Additionally, when the system detected the mismatch it activated a safety backoff that routed a subset of requests to a lower-throughput variant (rdw-base-1.1-quant), which has known higher latency for long sequences. That explains the spike in observed latency and 429s.
- Attached: quota_policy_snapshot.json and an annotated trace SUP-2143-incident-trace.pdf.

Mitigations applied at 10:05 PST:
- Reverted the cfg-20281106-quiet rollout for quota accounting on dedicated-pool-12 (temporary hotfix).
- Manually increased the instantaneous allowance for Streamline Health by 3x for the next 30 minutes while we stabilize.
- Enabled an emergency route to their primary pool instance (bypassing fallback) for critical customer requests.

Next steps:
- Engineering will schedule a controlled fix to unify the windowing logic and add a canary guard to prevent mixed-window rollouts.
- Product/Infra: review the rollout process to ensure per-customer reserved token logic is gated.

I will update the ticket with raw traces and the exact config diff.

— Neha
SRE, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
To: Jake Morris <jake.morris@streamlinehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.ai, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 7 Nov 2028 10:18:44 -0800
Subject: Re: Major latency spike + 429s impacting production (region: us-west)

Jake — quick update from triage (short version):
- Root cause: quota/burst window mismatch after a recent rollout; safety backoff routed some traffic to a lower-throughput model variant.
- Immediate mitigations: reverted the rollout for your pool, temporarily increased instantaneous allowance, and forced routing back to your primary pool.
- Impact: your QPS recovered to expected levels by ~10:12 PST; we've been monitoring for normal error rates since.

We're treating this as an incident and will provide a post-incident report (root cause + timeline + corrective actions) by end of day tomorrow. Marcus will follow up on any customer credits/contract impacts.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll keep you posted.

— Vivek

— Marissa
